extraFacts.fact: 316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 stainless steel; 316 contains molybdenum, which improves resistance to chlorides and pitting, so it is chosen for sea water, coastal plant and chloride-bearing process fluids.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A276 grade designations; Indus Hydraulics guide /blog/304-vs-316-stainless-steel-fittings

extraFacts.fact: Stainless steel threads can gall (seize and tear) when made up dry, so threads on stainless fittings are lubricated before assembly.

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies used for?
faqs.a: The Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies are 6" stainless steel floating flange assemblies in the Dixon Holedall series, with 150# ASA flange drilling, for the Holedall coupling system, which the maker describes as needing no bolts. The listing holds 3 part numbers.

faqs.q: How do I read part numbers such as R96P1LJR15?
faqs.a: The three numbers are R96P1LJR15, R96P2LJR15 and R96P3LJR15, which differ in the digit after P. The size table lists each only as a floating flange assembly and does not say what that digit selects, so give us your application and we confirm which number suits it.

faqs.q: What size are the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies?
faqs.a: The listing is 6" stainless steel, in 3 part numbers. The flange drilling is 150# ASA, so the flange mates with a 150# flange of the same size.

faqs.q: How do I choose between R96P1LJR15, R96P2LJR15 and R96P3LJR15?
faqs.a: The table gives the same description for all three, so choose by sending us the coupling or hose end you are fitting. The series is Holedall and the orientation is straight; the part number that matches your coupling is confirmed with the quotation.

faqs.q: What pressure do the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies hold?
faqs.a: The listing does not state a pressure rating, so we do not quote one. The flange drilling is 150# ASA; send the working pressure and temperature of your line and we confirm the assembly is suitable before you order.

faqs.q: What are the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives stainless steel and a 6" size. It does not state the grade, so send the grade you need, such as 304 or 316, and the fluid, and we confirm what is supplied before you order.

faqs.q: Which standards do the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies follow, and can I get certificates?
faqs.a: The listing names 150# ASA flange drilling and no separate standard or test certificate. If your job needs a material certificate or a flange standard, ask for it in the enquiry so it can be requested before supply.

faqs.q: What does the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies connect to?
faqs.a: The 150# ASA flange drilling bolts to a mating 150# flange of the same size, and the Holedall coupling system forms the joint without bolts. Send us the mating flange or coupling and we confirm the match.

faqs.q: How do I fit the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies?
faqs.a: The listing says the Holedall coupling system requires no bolts and gives a clean coupling with no protrusions. Follow the maker's fitting instructions for the coupling, and bolt the flange face to its 150# mate with a suitable gasket.

faqs.q: How do the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies differ from the SAE flange heads in this range?
faqs.a: The Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies have 150# ASA flange drilling, while the [stainless JIC 37° male × SAE Code 61 flange head](/p/stainless-steel-jic-37-male-x-sae-code-61-flange-head) and the other SAE flange heads in this range use four-bolt SAE Code 61 or 62 flanges. The two flange types do not bolt together.

faqs.q: Where do the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies come from?
faqs.a: The listing gives the country of origin as United States and the brand as Dixon Valve & Coupling. We ship worldwide from Dubai, and the commercial documents for your order state the origin and the customs code that apply.

faqs.q: Are the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies in stock, and how do I get a quotation?
faqs.a: Yes, the Dixon Floating Flange Assemblies is held in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and we ship worldwide with the best lead times. Quote the part numbers you need on [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is the Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head used for?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head is a straight flange head that joins a 37° JIC line to an SAE four-bolt flange port. It carries a male 37° JIC end and a male SAE Code 61 flange end in 316L stainless steel, forged, and this listing holds 18 part numbers from 1/2" to 2". Typical homes are offshore and marine lines, chemical and petroleum plant, and food and beverage process equipment.

faqs.q: How do I read part number IH-SS-1700-08-12 on the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head?
faqs.a: IH-SS-1700-08-12 reads as the base number IH-SS-1700 followed by one size code per port in order: 08 = 1/2" JIC 37° on end 1 and 12 = 3/4" Code 61 flange on end 2. The last row, IH-SS-1700-32-32, is 2" JIC 37° to 2" Code 61 flange. Quote the full number, or send the thread on each end and we will confirm it.

faqs.q: What sizes does the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head come in?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head is listed in 18 part numbers, 1/2" to 2". For example, IH-SS-1700-08-08 is 1/2" JIC 37° to 1/2" Code 61 flange; IH-SS-1700-16-32 is 1" JIC 37° to 2" Code 61 flange; IH-SS-1700-32-32 is 2" JIC 37° to 2" Code 61 flange. Sizes outside the table are quoted on request.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right size of JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head?
faqs.a: Choose the Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head by the thread on each end, then confirm the size code. Rows show 08 = 1/2" JIC 37° (3/4-16), 20 = 1-1/4" JIC 37° (1-5/8-12). Match the flange code (61 or 62) as well as the size.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure of the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head?
faqs.a: The manufacturer publishes no pressure rating for the Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head, so we do not quote one. Send the working pressure and temperature of your line and Indus engineering will confirm the fitting is suitable before you order. A mated pair is only as strong as its weakest end.

faqs.q: What is the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head made from, and when should I choose stainless over carbon steel?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head is made from 316L stainless steel, forged. 316L is the low-carbon grade of 316, which suits sea water and chloride-bearing service. Stainless is chosen where zinc-plated carbon steel would corrode, as in offshore and marine lines, chemical and petroleum plant, and food and beverage process equipment. The zinc-plated carbon steel version is listed separately as Male Flange Connector m JIC X L-series flange. Tell us the fluid and temperature if the medium is unusual.

faqs.q: Which standards does the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head follow, and can I get certificates?
faqs.a: The JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head is listed to SAE J514, ISO 8434-2, SAE J518, ISO 6162-1 and ASME B1.20.1. They cover 37° flared tube fittings, four-bolt flange connections, Code 61 flange heads and general-purpose inch pipe threads. This listing holds no test certificate or declaration; if your job needs a material certificate, ask for it in the enquiry so it can be requested before supply.

faqs.q: What does the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head connect to?
faqs.a: On the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head, the male 37° JIC end mates with a female 37° JIC swivel nut. For example a hose end or a flared tube held by a tube nut and sleeve. The Code 61 flange end bolts to a four-bolt port with Code 61 split flange halves. Matching parts: [Code 61 split flange kit](/p/stainless-steel-sae-code-61-split-flange-kit).

faqs.q: How do I install the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head without leaks or galling?
faqs.a: To fit the Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head: the 37° flare seats metal to metal, so fit it square, tighten to the maker's torque and do not add tape or sealant to the seat. Stainless threads can gall if made up dry, so lubricate them. See our [make-up torque guide](/blog/hydraulic-fitting-make-up-torque).

faqs.q: What is the difference between the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head and the JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head 45° Elbow?
faqs.a: The JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head and the [JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head 45° Elbow](/p/stainless-steel-jic-37-male-x-sae-code-61-flange-head-45-elbow) are listed as separate parts, so check which one your layout needs. The first is a straight flange head that joins a 37° JIC line to an SAE four-bolt flange port, with a male 37° JIC end and a male SAE Code 61 flange end; the second is a 45-degree elbow that joins a 37° JIC line to an SAE four-bolt flange port, with a male 37° JIC end and a male SAE Code 61 flange end. Choose by the line layout: this listing has 18 part numbers, 1/2" to 2".

faqs.a: Yes, the Stainless Steel JIC 37° Male × SAE Code 61 Flange Head is held in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and we ship worldwide with the best lead times. Quote the part numbers you need on [our contact page](/contact).
